meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (English common law foundation with indigenous fa'a Samoa customary law elements and modern commercial statutes)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: PACER Plus Economic Partnership Agreement (regional trade and investment facilitation)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 (No. 17 of 2007), as amended by the Money Laundering Prevention Amendment Act 2018; International Companies Act 1988 (No. 29 of 1988), as amended by the International Companies Amendment Act 2012; Companies Act 2001; Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism Regulations 2018; and binding directives of the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (confidential UBO register held by the Registrar of International Companies and the licensed registered agent; disclosure to the Financial Intelligence Unit and law enforcement upon lawful request)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour, Samoa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the Samoa Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade OR Consular Legalization via the nearest Samoa diplomatic mission

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour, Samoa

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency / Register of Directors and Officers
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Samoa notary public certification followed by Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the origin country's competent authority OR Consular Legalization by the nearest Samoa consular mission

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based client due diligence by the licensed registered agent, including PEP status identification, enhanced due diligence for PEPs and their family members/close associates, positive-matching screening against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and Samoa domestic sanctions designations; ongoing transaction monitoring and senior-management-approval gate for PEP onboarding.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa Companies Registry - International Companies Unit, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia, Samoa
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official languages are Samoan and English. An International Company name must be in Latin script (English or Samoan) and must end with 'Limited' or 'Ltd.'; non-Latin trading names (e.g., Chinese characters) are permitted only as a translated/transliterated secondary name recorded in the Memorandum of Association.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the licensed registered agent may file a written administrative appeal with the Registrar of International Companies within 21 calendar days, attaching grounds for statutory eligibility and any requisite ministerial or Central Bank of Samoa consent; the Registrar shall issue a determination within 14 working days; a further appeal lies to the Minister of Commerce, Industry and Labour within 15 calendar days of the Registrar's decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as the sole registered office; an International Company must maintain a physical registered office in Samoa at the licensed registered agent's address. Virtual/back-office arrangements may supplement but not replace this statutory presence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for a Low_Risk_Standard trading structure - estimated unannounced inspection probability of approximately 5% per annum; likelihood increases substantially upon generation of sanctions or PEP adverse alerts.

Notarization and apostille/consular legalization of corporate documents

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended; principally sections 4 (incorporation), 7-8 (memorandum and articles), 13 (application), 87 (registered office), 89 (registered agent), and 174 (exemptions from domestic licensing)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International and Foreign Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Apia, Samoa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation (Form 1) together with notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association (constitutional documents)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital and no escrow or capital deposit requirement; authorized capital may be as low as USD 1, with shares issued at par or no-par value and consideration may be unpaid or deferred
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the subscription by the Subscriber of One Ordinary Share of USD 1 for the International Company be and is hereby accepted, and that the issuance of that share in the capital of the Company is approved. RESOLVED FURTHER that the registered office of the Company be established at the office of the licensed registered agent, Apia, Samoa, pursuant to Section 87 of the International Companies Act 1987. RESOLVED FURTHER that [Director Name] and [Secretary Name] be appointed as first Director and Corporate Secretary respectively, to serve until removed by the Board. RESOLVED FURTHER that the Director be authorised to open merchant payment accounts (Shopify Payments, Stripe) and bank accounts, execute resolutions, and adopt the corporate seal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Legal Cleanliness Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International and Foreign Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) — via a licensed registered agent in Apia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage an SIFA-licensed company manager to submit a name enquiry to the Companies Registry for the proposed corporate name incorporating the suffix 'Limited'. Obtain written name clearance confirming no conflict with existing International or domestic companies and no prohibited or misleading terms.
required_dossiers: Engagement letter with licensed registered agent
Name enquiry form
Declaration of no prohibited words in the proposed name
Identity and KYC questionnaire of the proposed shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or placed on requisition, the agent files two alternative names for assessment; no additional government filing fee is charged for the resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Execution and Notarization of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public / licensed attorney; constitution ultimately approved by SIFA
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Memorandum and Articles of Association compliant with sections 7-8 of the International Companies Act 1987, stating the company name, objects (designer toy design, contract manufacturing, intellectual property licensing, worldwide sales and distribution of vinyl collectibles), share capital clause with no minimum paid-up capital, and election to issue no-par shares. The sole subscriber executes the constitution in the presence of a notary, who affixes a notarial certificate.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association (draft and executed)
Shareholder subscription consent
Notarized passport copy of the subscriber
Consent of proposed director and corporate secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries the objects or capital clause, revise the relevant provision and re-execute before the notary, then file a supplementary statement with the Registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Application for Incorporation with SIFA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International and Foreign Companies (SIFA), Apia, Samoa
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Application for Incorporation (Form 1) at the SIFA registry counters or through the licensed agent's electronic filing portal, attaching the notarized constitution, declaration of compliance, consent of the registered agent and the registered office consent. Pay the government filing fee of USD 100 plus applicable stamp duty, and retain the stamped receipt.
required_dossiers: Application for Incorporation (Form 1)
Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Declaration of compliance signed by the subscriber
Consent of registered agent and registered office consent form
Government fee remittance record
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is requisitioned, fully respond within 14 days by amending the application and re-filing; an expedited ('same-day') process is available upon payment of an additional SIFA fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Corporate Kit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar (SIFA) and the newly formed International Company's first Board
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation bearing the company registration number. The licensed agent prepares the corporate kit comprising the common seal, share certificates, share register, director and officer registers, and the statutory minute book. The Board approves the issuance of the subscriber's share certificate.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Consent-to-act forms of director and corporate secretary
Share certificate template for the ordinary share
Order form for corporate kit and common seal
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate of Incorporation contains any typographical or substantive error, file a rectification application with the Registrar; the corrected certificate is issued within 3 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Governance Filings and Banking Arrangements
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors; licensed registered agent; commercial banks in Samoa (e.g., ANZ Samoa, Bank of South Pacific) and payment processor compliance teams
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting by written resolution to appoint officers, adopt the registered office, and approve banking and merchant account mandates. File the register of directors and officers and any beneficial ownership declaration under the Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Regulations with the Registrar. Submit corporate documents to banks and payment processors (Shopify Payments, Stripe, local POS) for merchant account activation, including CRS/FATCA self-certification.
required_dossiers: First board written resolution
Register of directors and corporate secretary
Beneficial ownership register and declaration forms
CRS/FATCA self-certification forms for the beneficial owner
Bank account application and merchant onboarding forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries beneficial ownership records, provide a corrected declaration within 7 days; if a bank or payment processor issues a KYC query, supply apostilled constitutional documents and notarized identity evidence for re-review.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) – Trade and Commerce Division (Business Licenses) and Labour Division (Occupational Safety and Health); Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) for International Company operational approvals
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business License (Manufacturing – Toys and Collectibles) under the Business Licenses Act 1998; where the International Company elects to conduct physical manufacturing in Samoa, a domestic market access endorsement under the International Companies Act 1987 is additionally required

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA), Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Samoa
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Class 2 – Registration with Environmental Management Plan (EMP) and Development Consent under the Planning and Urban Management Act 2004; full Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) is not required for ISIC 3240 light manufacturing occupying less than 500 m² floor area with no hazardous discharge
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Effluent: Water Resources Management Act 2008 consent limits – pH 6.0-9.0, BOD5 ≤ 50 mg/L, TSS ≤ 50 mg/L, oil and grease ≤ 10 mg/L; Air: VOC emissions from airbrushing and solvent use controlled by local extraction and filtration units with workplace threshold ≤ 50 ppm; Waste: resin, paint thinners and isocyanate waste manifested and transported only by licensed carriers under the Waste Management Act 2008, with certificates of disposal retained
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (SFESA) after on-site inspection covering means of egress, extinguishers and alarm systems; structural load inspection and building compliance certificate for storage mezzanines; occupational safety and health workplace registration and industrial hygiene clearance from the MCIL Labour Division prior to commencement of production

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Samoa Revenue Authority (SRA) — the integrated tax and customs administration for Samoa; taxpayer services accessible through the SRA e-Tax online portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign person incorporating a Samoa International Company (IC) must appoint a licensed registered agent. The agent submits the incorporation documents to the Samoa International Companies Office. Following incorporation, the agent files an application with the SRA for a Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) on behalf of the IC, attaching the Certificate of Incorporation, registered office address, and details of directors/shareholders. The IC is tax-exempt and is not required to obtain a VAGST registration unless it undertakes local taxable supplies, but a TIN is issued for administrative and financial purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No Samoa domestic check-the-box or pass-through election is available for an International Company; the entity is a taxable exempt body corporate under the International Companies Act. Foreign shareholders may apply home-country classification rules (e.g., U.S. Form 8832) subject to hybrid mismatch rules under OECD/G20 BEPS standards.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: 40,000 WST of annual taxable turnover (economic threshold triggering mandatory VAGST registration)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Samoa does not currently mandate real-time fiscal clearance, API-linked e-invoicing, or government digital stamping. Registered taxpayers may file VAGST returns electronically through the SRA e-Tax portal, but there is no automated clearance gateway for invoices or customs validation.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The export of goods from Samoa, and the supply of services to a recipient outside Samoa, qualify for the 0% VAGST rate where the supplier is a registered VAGST person and retains the required documentary evidence. An International Company conducting offshore trade is outside the Samoan tax net; any incidental local supplies remain taxable unless zero-rated for export.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent zero-rating claims and false export documentation may be disallowed by the SRA, resulting in retrospective VAT assessments, penalties, and interest at statutory rates. Criminal liability may arise under the Customs Act and VAGST legislation, with fines up to WST 1,000,000, imprisonment of directors, and forfeiture of goods or benefits.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Samoa operates a managed float for the Samoan Tala (WST) under the Exchange Control Act 1976 and the Central Bank of Samoa Act 1984. The capital account is restricted: all non-resident direct and portfolio investments, and all external borrowings, require prior Exchange Control approval from the Central Bank of Samoa. Current account transactions, including trade-related payments and profit remittances, are generally permitted upon submission of documentary evidence, but repatriation of dividends, branch profits, and liquidation proceeds requires certification of source of funds, tax clearance from the Ministry for Revenue, and a valid Overseas Investment approval. The International Company (IC) regime, governed by the International Companies Act 1987, provides statutory exchange control exemptions for international companies holding a valid Tax Exempt Zone certificate and conducting business exclusively outside Samoa; such entities may operate foreign-currency-denominated accounts and remit profits freely without Central Bank approval. However, any physical conversion into WST, local disbursement, or establishment of a Samoan-dollar account triggers standard convertibility controls. Profit remittance hurdles are minimal for pure offshore IC treasury operations, but onshore subsidiaries or entities with Samoan-source revenue face a refundable withholding tax regime and must substantiate arm's length charges and audited financial statements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: The Exchange Control Act 1976 imposes a statutory obligation on residents to offer export proceeds for conversion to WST within 90 days of receipt, or such period as the Central Bank of Samoa may approve. For non-resident-owned International Companies operating under the International Companies Act 1987, the surrender and conversion requirement does not apply, provided the IC is not a 'resident' under the Exchange Control Act and the proceeds relate exclusively to offshore activities. The mandatory conversion ratio is effectively 100% for resident exporters and 0% for qualified ICs with non-resident ownership and offshore conduct. Documentary requirements for non-applicability include an Exchange Control exemption certificate, tax exemption certificate, and audited confirmations that sales were concluded outside Samoa and settled in foreign currency.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account / Foreign Currency Account
Operational Account / Foreign Currency Account / Cross-Border Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-High for non-WST operating currencies, Low for WST-denominated accounts. Samoa does not have a domestic EMI licensing framework; therefore offshore digital EMIs (e.g., BaaS platforms in Hong Kong, Singapore, or the UK) may be used by the Samoan International Company as foreign-currency treasury and payment settlement rails only if: (1) the EMI does not hold itself out as a Samoan bank, (2) the IC maintains its offshore tax-exempt status and non-resident ownership, (3) no Samoan-source receipts flow into the EMI account, and (4) the Central Bank of Samoa has not issued a marketing or solicitation prohibition in respect of that EMI. The 1987 International Companies Act is permissive as to opening accounts outside Samoa; however, banks and EMIs will typically require a certificate of good standing, register of directors, share register, and compliance with their own AML/KYC rules. Viability is reduced for EMIs that require a local office, directorship KYC interviews, or a Samoan physical nexus. No PSD2-style open-banking or local EMI passport exists in Samoa.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not statutorily mandatory for International Company account opening at Bank of Samoa, ANZ, or BSP Samoa, provided the ultimate beneficial owners are already onboarded through an approved correspondent bank or a licensed introducing entity. In practice, ANZ and BSP apply global group KYC policies: at least one director or an authorized signatory must attend an in-person or video-conference identification interview; full remote opening is possible only where the IC has pre-existing banking relationships with the same banking group and the KYC profile is categorised as Low_Risk_Standard under the FATF-style risk taxonomy. Samoa's AML/CFT Act 2021 and the Central Bank of Samoa KYC Guidelines require all directors and 10%+ shareholders to submit certified passport copies, proof of residential address, source of wealth for any inbound capital injection exceeding USD 10,000 equivalent, and a board resolution ratifying the account opening. For the Collector Toys / Designer Blind Box segment, no local interview is required if the onboarding is handled through a Hong Kong or Singapore relationship branch of the same banking group.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity arising from bearer-like share structures or nominee shareholders in the Samoan International Company
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete registered agent certificate; full legal and beneficial ownership chain to natural persons; certified copies of passports and shareholder registers; signed declaration identifying all 10%+ beneficial owners; audited financial statements or an accountant certified capital introduction letter proving legitimate source of funds from toy merchandise sales or parental working capital; no bearer share certificate in circulation (confirmed by registered agent).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Screening hit from OFAC, EU, UN, or SAMOA sanctions list against a designer/brand owner, distributor, or counterparty in the blind box supply chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanction screening of all principals against SAMOA (Central Bank of Samoa sanctions list), UN, EU, US OFAC, and UK HMT lists; negative screening report dated within 90 days; corroborative KYC documents for each screened party; contractual evidence showing the IP/designer is an arm's length third-party licensor; written compliance attestation from the bank's appointed compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction nexus: royalty payments to Hong Kong, China, or Singapore, coupled with physical goods routed through mainland China manufacturing
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Export trade documents (commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading/air waybill, Cargo Importer Export Declaration), full manufacturing and logistics chain mapping, proof that the Samoan IC only acts as merchant/licensor and not as manufacturer; copy of the tax-exempt certificate; transfer pricing documentation for any intercompany royalty; underlying IP license agreement and designer commission schedule.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexpected inbound funding exceeding 10,000 USD from non-banking channels (crypto, e-wallet, affiliate payout)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source of funds file consisting of payout ledger from Shopify Payments/Stripe, order-level revenue report, audited annual accounts, intercompany loan agreement in writing, and a signed source-of-funds declaration; if e-wallet/crypto was used, provide withdrawal confirmation, blockchain forensic report, and a bank-approved conversion chain from the EMI to the Samoan IC.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Discrepancy between declared business scope 'ISIC 3240' (Toys/Collectibles) and indistinguishable 'designer gambling/blind box' probabilistic mechanics (loot-box risk)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Consumer-facing terms and conditions showing no random reward value above fair purchase price; legal memorandum (issued by Samoan or Singapore counsel) confirming the blind box mechanics are a sales promotional feature and not gambling under Samoan Gaming Act; evidence that each box has fixed minimum collectible content; age-gating controls and a compliance opinion from the designer IP owner.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections into the Samoan International Company should route exclusively through the international banking network in USD, HKD, or SGD using MT103 wire transfers with bank reference 'BEPS' (Beneficiary is the Samoan IC). Permissible purpose codes: EGR (acquisition/sale of shares), EIA (investment income), EBP (operating expenses), or P01 (trade-related advance) depending on the sending jurisdiction; for the USA use FFIEC BSA purpose code 'DF' / 'C11' with narrative 'share capital contribution to offshore IC'; for Hong Kong use TMA 'ID' (intercompany funding); for Singapore use MAS 'EC' (equity capital). Verification requirements: inward remittance advice, commercial invoice, share subscription agreement, board resolution, and a certificate of non-resident status. The Central Bank of Samoa does not require pre-approval for IC foreign currency accounts, but the receiving bank will require a copy of the IC's tax exemption certificate and confirmation that the funds do not represent proceeds of Samoan domestic sales. A minimum of USD 1 or equivalent is accepted; no minimum capital requirement exists under the International Companies Act 1987. Internal loan capital routed via a shareholder loan must be evidenced by a written loan agreement and may be repatriated under the same MT103 channel with purpose code 'IRP' (intra-group repayment).
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements to manufacturers, licensors, logistic providers, and resellers must be settled via SWIFT MT103 standard wire transfers from the IC's offshore foreign-currency account, using beneficiary bank details in China, Hong Kong, or Singapore. Purpose codes: 'TCR' (trade payable), 'ROY' (royalty/license fee), 'COM' (commission), or 'ADD' (advertising and distribution). For larger purchase orders exceeding USD 50,000, a clean Commercial Letter of Credit (L/C at sight) may be issued by the Samoan IC's bank through a correspondent bank; however, most designer toy transactions are effectively settled through MT103 because intermediary banks and Chinese beneficiaries prefer telegraphic transfer due to low transaction amount and rapid clearance. The use of the Samoan IC as an offshore merchant intermediary does not require Central Bank approval if no WST conversion occurs. All outbound wires must append the Samoan IC name as legal entity, tax identification number or certified IC registration number, and the purpose code. Invoices must reference the purchase order number and the ISIC 3240 description. Clearing rails available: SWIFT MT103 direct, MT202 COVER for high-value settlement through a nostro account, Commercial L/C for documentary trade, and digital wallet/EMI bulk payout (e.g., Payoneer, Airwallex, or Wise Business) for payments below USD 10,000 to suppliers/creators; note that domestic POS rails in Samoa (local EFT/POS) are irrelevant to the offshore IC treasury architecture.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright forwards on USD/WST, HKD/USD, SGD/USD, and CNY/USD through an internationally licensed counterparty, only where the IC has a demonstrable short-term WST exposure (unlikely for pure offshore operations).

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing WST (offshore USD/WST NDF market is exceptionally thin) or CNY (onshore/offshore CNH deliverable forwards, not WST NDF), permitted for ICs hedging expected Chinese RMB settlement obligations.

Cross-currency swaps between USD and HKD or USD and SGD, executed under an ISDA Master Agreement with a global bank, permitted without Central Bank of Samoa approval, provided the swap proceeds settle outside Samoa.

Vanilla FX options (call/put on USD/CNY or USD/HKD) for hedging purchase order payable obligations; speculative or uncovered options are prohibited by most international banks and subject to negative KYC treatment.

Currency swaps between WST and USD, only under Central Bank of Samoa Exchange Control approval, with documentary proof of underlying trade exposure; this is generally not recommended for an offshore IC.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Registration / Licence Fee Renewal under the International Companies Act 1987, payable through the licensed registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payable on the anniversary of incorporation; the SIFA renewal invoice must be settled by the due date shown on the invoice, normally the last day of the month preceding the incorporation anniversary.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment triggers prescribed late penalties under the International Companies (Fees) Regulations; continued non-payment may lead to administrative strike-off under the International Companies Act 1987 after the statutory notice period.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Confirmation / Annual Return; exempt International Companies are not required to file audited financial statements with this return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after each anniversary of incorporation; if the anniversary falls in a closure period, the filing is accepted on the next business day.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts a prescribed penalty per month or part thereof; persistent default is a statutory ground for administrative strike-off and may require court/Registrar restoration with outstanding fees and penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Annual Confirmation / UBO Register Audit lodged with the annual confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed Samoa registered agent, acting for the Registrar of International Companies and Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually together with the corporate confirmation return; any change in beneficial ownership during the year must be recorded in the UBO register and notified to the registered agent within 14 days of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance is an offence under Samoa's AML/CFT framework and may result in monetary penalties imposed by the Financial Intelligence Unit; false or omitted filings may also support administrative strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory independent audit applies to an ordinary exempt International Company irrespective of turnover or assets, unless: (a) it is licensed under financial services, banking, insurance, or trust legislation; (b) its articles of association require an audit; (c) shareholders holding at least 10% of voting rights request an audit; or (d) the Registrar or a court orders an audit for regulatory or public-interest reasons.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: If financial statements are prepared, Samoa applies IFRS as adopted by the national accounting framework; IFRS for SMEs is acceptable for private entities. The International Companies Act requires accounting records that sufficiently explain transactions and financial position but does not prescribe a public chart of accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each International Company must maintain a Register of Beneficial Owners identifying every individual holding or controlling, directly or indirectly, more than 25% of shares or voting rights, or otherwise exercising ultimate control. On each annual confirmation, the Samoa registered agent must audit and certify the register. Share transfers require director approval under the articles, updating of the Register of Members, and recording of the new beneficial owner within 14 days. The register remains confidential but must be produced to SIFA or the Financial Intelligence Unit on lawful demand.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Shareholder and Director Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 – USD 1,000 per year, depending on the licensed Samoa registered agent and inclusive of registered office service and filing compliance support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not applicable for an exempt International Company; a voluntary certified audit by a licensed Samoan auditor is typically USD 2,500 – USD 7,500 per engagement

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% (Samoa International Company tax-exempt status); standard domestic headline corporate rate is 27%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The Samoa International Company (IC) enjoys a statutory total exemption from income tax, withholding tax, capital gains tax, and stamp duty on worldwide income, including distributions, interest, royalties, and proceeds of sale of shares. No payroll taxes apply to non-resident directors or shareholders of the IC. This exemption is contingent upon strict adherence to the International Companies Act and the absence of domestic Samoa-source trading activity.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No Corporate Income Tax Return is required for a Samoa International Company. Annual compliance is limited to the Annual Return form AR-INT filed through the Samoa International Companies Registry (SIFA e-Registry / online agent portal).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (filed by or before the anniversary of incorporation)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The AR-INT Annual Return must be lodged no later than the anniversary date of the IC's incorporation, together with the prescribed annual government fee. No CIT return deadline applies because the IC is tax-exempt.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered legal name, International Company number, date of incorporation, registered office address in Samoa.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident beneficial owners must ensure the company name appears exactly as on the certificate of incorporation; registered office must be at the approved registered agent's address in Apia.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section B – Registered Agent and Secretary
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name, address, and licence number of the Samoan registered agent and company secretary.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders may not serve as the registered agent; the agent must be licensed by the Samoa International Companies Registrar.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full legal names, nationality, residential addresses, and shareholding details of all directors and shareholders.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete this section with certified passport copies and an up-to-date service address; non-resident individuals may validly hold all directorships.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section D – Declaration of IC Tax-Exempt Status
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration that the IC has not conducted any Samoa-source trading activity and does not hold Samoan land or operate a local business.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The declaration must be signed by the non-resident director or authorised agent; false declarations expose the IC to immediate loss of exemption and criminal penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section E – Annual Government Fee Calculation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of the annual government fee based on issued share capital, filed share returns, and any applicable late penalties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The fee is typically paid by the registered agent on behalf of the non-resident shareholder; proof of remittance should be retained.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the AR-INT Annual Return attracts an automatic late fee of WST 500 and a monthly surcharge of WST 50. Continued default leads to a notice of striking-off, dissolution of the IC, restoration costs, and disqualification of the registered agent. Where a false declaration is used to retain the tax exemption, the Commissioner of Revenue may impose a further penalty equal to 100% of taxes that would otherwise have been payable, plus default interest and potential criminal prosecution.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for dividends paid by a Samoa International Company to non-resident shareholders. Dividends paid by a standard Samoa domestic company to a non-resident are subject to a statutory withholding tax of 20%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Because an IC's distributions are entirely exempt from Samoan withholding tax, a treaty relief application is ordinarily unnecessary. Should a treaty partner impose a foreign withholding tax, or should a limited Samoan-sourced payment inadvertently arise, the administrative protocol requires: (1) filing Form WHT-DTA with the Samoa Ministry of Revenue; (2) submitting a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the Samoan Revenue Administration, supported by the IC's certificate of incorporation, board resolution, and confirmation of economic substance; (3) providing the payer with the approved relief notice before remittance. TRCs for ICs are issued restrictively and only where the Commissioner is satisfied that the IC is a substantive tax resident of Samoa and not a shell conduit.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties and interest paid by a Samoa International Company to non-residents: 0% statutory rate under the International Companies Act. For standard domestic companies, the statutory non-resident withholding tax rates are 20% for interest and 20% for royalties, subject to reduction under applicable Samoan Double Tax Agreements (typically to 5% on royalties and 10% on interest where the beneficial owner qualifies).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No threshold is imposed on a tax-exempt Samoa International Company; it is outside the transfer pricing documentation net. A taxable Samoan enterprise, by contrast, must prepare contemporaneous Local File and Master File documentation in accordance with the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines when aggregate annual related-party turnover exceeds WST 15,000,000.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Samoa International Companies (Economic Substance) Regulations 2018 impose economic substance obligations only where the IC carries on a 'relevant activity' specifically defined as: banking, insurance, financing, leasing, fund management, distribution and service centres, shipping, and intellectual property holding. A designer blind-box toys entity engaged in genuine manufacturing, online merchandising, and direct-to-consumer sales through Shopify Payments, Stripe, or Local POS is not ordinarily engaged in a 'distribution and service centre' activity because the latter targets related-party distribution arrangements. However, the IC must maintain a real physical presence, adequate employees, accurate accounting records, and board control in Samoa if it claims to be a participant in such activities; otherwise the exemption may be disregarded and the IC recharacterised as a shell.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: An IC that, despite conducting a real e-commerce business and earning income through foreign payment processors, signs a false declaration that it has no Samoan-source revenue, fails to disclose that the management and control of the business is exercised within Samoa, or continues to claim the 0% exemption without satisfying the economic substance condition. The use of Chinese-language contracts and family trust structures to mask the beneficial owner's actual commercial activities further aggravates the offence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: A fine of up to WST 1,000,000 or 100% of the tax evaded, whichever is greater, plus default interest and reinstatement of all unpaid taxes for the period during which the exemption was improperly claimed. Criminal conviction under Samoa's Tax Administration Act 2012 carries imprisonment of up to 7 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced where the IC is proven to be an agent, alter ego, or sham vehicle of the director. Directors become personally liable for all unpaid tax, civil penalties, and restitution of diverted profits. The court may impose travel bans, asset freezing orders, and disqualification from managing any company for up to 10 years; imprisonment is automatic upon conviction for willful evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Sham Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the Samoa IC as a mere paper company with no office, no employees, no accounting records, and no board function, while using its bank accounts and payment gateways (Shopify Payments, Stripe, Local POS) to launder designer-toy sales proceeds for undisclosed Chinese principals or to extract treaty benefits on behalf of non-resident sellers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Registrar may strike off the IC, revoke its certificate of incorporation, and impose administrative penalties under the International Companies (Economic Substance) Regulations. The Ministry of Revenue may recharacterise the entire income stream in the hands of the ultimate beneficial owner and levy the standard 27% corporate rate plus 20% withholding tax, together with a 100% civil penalty for gross negligence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Beneficial owners and directors who execute false declarations are jointly and severally liable for all taxes, penalties, and restitution. Courts may issue a 'Continental Indemnity' style asset tracing order against personal bank accounts, enforce personal guarantees on merchant processing agreements, and order passport surrender pending full payment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Allowing the designer-toy sales proceeds to flow through the IC without maintaining a register of beneficial owners, conducting customer due diligence on wholesale buyers and family trust settlors, or filing suspicious transaction reports when payments originate from high-risk or sanctioned entities. Routing funds via multiple jurisdictions and immediate payout to non-resident individuals constitutes a prohibited laundering pattern.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Samoa's Money Laundering and Proceeds of Crime Act and the AML/CFT Regulations, the enforcement agency may impose a penalty of up to WST 750,000 per violation on the company, confiscate the designer-toy inventory and bank balances, and impose imprisonment of up to 7 years on the compliance officer for willful non-compliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the designated Money Laundering Reporting Officer face criminal prosecution, confiscation of personal property, and bankruptcy orders. Where the director knowingly allows the IC to be used for laundering, the court will pierce the veil and hold the director personally liable for the full value of laundered funds, with potential extradition under mutual legal assistance treaties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate Fraud and False Statutory Filing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Falsifying the AR-INT Annual Return, forging director or shareholder consents, issuing shares without consideration to conceal control by a Chinese-family trust, or providing misleading ownership information to payment processors and banks to secure merchant accounts and evade taxation in the beneficial owner's jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Samoa's Crimes Act, conviction for false corporate filing or forgery attracts a fine of up to WST 200,000, restitution orders, and imprisonment of up to 5 years. Civil courts may order fraudulent trading compensation to creditors and compulsory winding-up of the IC.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for all debts incurred during fraudulent trading. A court may also declare the director personally liable to repay all amounts wrongfully extracted through the IC, prohibit the director from incorporating any new company in Samoa, and issue a bench warrant or travel ban for non-appearance at regulatory hearings.
